Blotter / Privacy policy

Your rules.
On your iPhone.

How Blotter handles your information.

Last updated November 3, 2026 · Developer: droessmj

At a glance

Blotter: Message Filter is an iPhone app developed by droessmj. It filters eligible texts from unknown senders using keywords you choose. It requires no account and uses no advertising, tracking, or third-party analytics SDKs.

On-device message processing

When you enable Blotter in iPhone Settings, iOS supplies eligible incoming SMS/MMS messages to its filter extension. The filter compares the message text with your saved keywords and matching options on your iPhone, then returns a classification to iOS.

Message text is not sent to the developer or a developer-operated server. The filter does not use the sender field. Blotter does not save message bodies, senders, message timestamps, filter decisions, or a history of keyword matches.

Information stored on your iPhone

Blotter stores your configured keywords, matching options, and setup status in shared app preferences so the app and its filter can use your rules. These preferences may be included in device backups according to your Apple settings.

The developer does not receive your rules or message data from the app. They are not sold or shared with advertising or analytics services.

Retention, deletion, and disabling the filter

Keyword rules stay in app storage until you remove them. You can stop future filtering by deselecting Blotter in the text message filtering settings under iPhone Settings → Apps → Messages.

Using Delete App removes that app’s private local storage; offloading preserves app data. Shared rules may remain while another installed app uses the same shared group. Device backups are managed separately through Apple’s controls. Blotter does not control messages retained in Apple’s Messages app.

Activity logging has been removed. Blotter deletes accessible legacy shared files and Keychain activity without reading their contents, while keeping your rules and matching options. Cleanup failures are retried; the app reports failures it encounters. Generic cleanup diagnostics contain no sender, keyword, or message body.

Blotter now has a separate app and filter identity from older Sift development builds. It retains the existing shared rule storage, but cannot access the old app’s or filter’s private containers. Its filter can delete only its own private legacy log. After confirming your rules in Blotter and selecting the new filter in Settings, remove the old installation to remove its private local files. Previously exported copies and old backups must be managed separately.

When you contact support

Issues and feature requests are handled in the app repository on GitHub. GitHub processes your account information and anything you submit under its own privacy policy. In a public repository, issues and comments are public: your username, message, and attachments can be read by others. Do not post private habit records, real texts, verification codes, or phone numbers.

If you email instead, the developer receives your email address and the information you choose to include. This is used to answer your request, troubleshoot issues, and handle follow-up correspondence. Email is processed by the email providers involved in delivery and storage.

Support correspondence is retained as needed to resolve your request and maintain relevant correspondence, or as required by law. You can use the contact below to ask about or request deletion of information you sent to support. Please do not send private habit records, real message contents, verification codes, or phone numbers unless necessary and discussed first.

This support website

This website uses Google Analytics to understand visits and how its pages are used. It uses the same Google Analytics measurement ID as droessmj.com. Google receives information such as pages visited, browser and device details, and network information; analytics cookies can recognize returning browsers and may be shared across droessmj.com subdomains. This website analytics is separate from the iPhone apps, which do not include Google Analytics or send habit data, keyword rules, or message contents to it.

Google processes analytics information under its Privacy Policy. Analytics retention and related settings are managed in the shared Google Analytics property. You can block analytics with browser controls or use the Google Analytics opt-out browser add-on where supported. For questions or deletion requests about information sent through this website, use the privacy contact below. The site loads no third-party fonts or embedded media. Email links open your chosen mail app; no message is sent until you send it.

The website is hosted on GitHub Pages. GitHub logs visitors’ IP addresses for security purposes. This is separate from data processed by the iPhone app. See GitHub Pages data collection and the GitHub Privacy Statement.
